Consumer complaint narrative:
Dear Capital Management Services , LP, I am writing to formally request both verification and validation of the alleged debt you claim I owe, in accordance with my rights under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), Section 809 ( b ). Verification and validation are distinct legal concepts, and I demand that you provide both.

Verification is the process of confirming whether I actually owe the debt, as referenced in Chaudhry v. Gallerizzo, 174 F.3d 394 ( 4th Cir. 1999 ). According to Blacks Law Dictionary, verification is defined as an averment that the party pleading is ready to establish the truth of what he has set forth. The examination of a writing for the purpose of ascertaining its truth ; or a certificate or affidavit that it is true. In McDonald v. Rosengarten, 134 Ill. 126, 25 N.E. ( 1890 ), the court explained that verification involves the " confirmation of the correctness, truth, or authenticity of a pleading, account, or other paper, by an affidavit, oath, or deposition. '' Other courts, such as in Summerfield v. Phoenix Assur. Co. ( C. C. ) 65 Fed. 296 ( 1922 ) and Patterson v. Brooklyn, 6 App. Div. 127, 40 N.Y. Supp. 581 ( 1898 ), have reiterated this legal principle. 

Therefore, I request the following : Proof that I am legally responsible for the debt in question. A verified statement of the original creditor and the contract or agreement that created the debt.

Validation is necessary to confirm the legitimacy of this debt before any further action can be taken, as referenced in Spears v. Brennan, 745 N.E. 2d 862 Ind. App. ( 2001 ). Black 's Law Dictionary defines validation as assessing an action to determine it is complete, correct, implemented, and delivering the correct outcome. Oxford defines it as to check or prove the validity or accuracy of something, and Merriam-Webster explains it as to show the existence or truth of, by evidence. 

To this end, I am requesting that you provide : Validation of the debt, including a breakdown of how the amount was calculated, itemizing any interest, fees, or charges added to the original balance.

Documentation proving that your agency is authorized to collect the debt on behalf of the original creditor. Any judgment or legal order obtained against me regarding this debt ( if applicable ). Proof that the debt is not time-barred under the statute of limitations in my state.

Until you provide both verification and validation of the debt, I request that you cease all collection activities, including reporting this alleged debt to any credit reporting agencies, as required by the FDCPA.

Please respond with the requested information within 30 days of receipt of this letter. If you can not provide the necessary verification and validation, I expect you to remove any record of this debt and cease all collection efforts.

Thank you for your immediate attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving the proper documentation. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

My overall concern is about the unfair and unjust business practice from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. 
It involves the revocation of my access to their credit card called XXXX XXXX. This credit card was not terminated because of missed payments on the account. I, as the customer, was told by a collections account XXXX named XXXX that they terminated the card because of a late payment towards a car loan I have with the XXXX XXXX. XXXX told me a portion of my past due balance on the car loan was 45 days past due so they closed my credit card account, that was in good standing. They mailed me an adverse action letter with a handwritten date of XX/XX/XXXX. I was able to payoff the total past due balance on the car loan on XX/XX/XXXX, by phone, with the same account XXXX named XXXX, who did not mention the termination of my credit card. XXXX the past due payment brought my car loan current and at that point meant I had about XXXX more payments to make before its completely paid off. As of the date of this complaint, I have about XXXX payments left, with a balance of about {$900.00} on the car loan. 
So, my car loan is current, but the XXXX XXXX credit card will now be reported as closed by the creditor but not because of any default issues, but because of a past due payment on a car loan, that as I stated before, is no longer in any past due status. 

They say they have the right to do this, but my concern is they will continue to report this credit card to credit agencies based on misrepresentation. The credit card will remain on credit reports as adversely closed but only based on the auto loan which is currently not in arrears. Also, the balance of my credit card is significantly higher at about {$5000.00}. And as I stated, to date, the car loan balance is {$900.00}. I will be finished paying off the car loan in XXXX, but I will still have to pay off the credit card balance that no longer functions as a credit card, due to it being closed based on what will be a faulty status because the car loan will be paid off. 
So, in other words, it seems like this tactic is an excessive penalty that transfers the moment in time I had a past due amount on the car loan, to be paid off in perpetuity through payments on the credit card. 
Why I say in perpetuity is because my auto loan is a fixed installment loan while the credit card inherently has higher fees and longer duration to pay off. The auto loan is collateral based while the credit card is unsecured. And the credit card was terminated when it was at a high balance of {$5000.00}. 
It seems like a horribly unjust, if not illegal, way to abruptly close a consumer 's credit card account with a balance, but with no notice and then cite that it has nothing to do with my standing with the credit card but with another product that had the past due issue resolved and has a nominal balance remaining. 
I told them this was my first time working with a credit union, as I've never experienced a bank try to retaliate on a consumer being behind on a car loan by shutting down their credit card and expecting them to still pay it off. 
I'm not sure what legal action I can take, but I wanted this to be exposed as consumers are supposed to have protections from wicked actions. 
I believe I will have to find some legal representation because I refuse to let XXXX XXXX  extort money out of me as a business practice.

'' Wanting to be cooperative and professional right before beginning the role, I provided it. 

Shortly after, I received text messages from an unknown number pretending to be the CEO. The sender said they needed help with a confidential " quick errand '' to surprise staff with gift cards for good work, emphasized not telling anyone to avoid ruining the surprise, and created intense urgency by implying it was time-sensitive and only I could assist. Starting around XXXX XXXX  the same day, the sender directed me to buy gift cards immediately, beginning with XXXX {$200.00} XXXX cards and escalating to more.

This is a proven scam induced by impersonation and deception, exploiting well-documented psychological vulnerabilities : the pressure of starting a new job, fear of disappointing a new employer, chaos of relocating, and urgency tactics designed to bypass rational thinking. Consumer complaint narrative:
I am submitting this complaint regarding XXXX continued reporting of a rental debt that is inaccurate, previously deleted by another consumer reporting agency, and paid in full through a government rental assistance program. 

The account in question is a rental debt that was paid in full by Texas Rent Relief, a government-administered emergency rental assistance program. Once payment was issued, I was no longer legally obligated for the balance. There is no remaining consumer liability. 

Despite this, XXXX  continues to report the account after repeated disputes, while XXXX  has permanently deleted the same account after determining that it could not be verified as belonging to me and/or could not be validated. 

XXXX continued reporting violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) for the following reasons : 1. Violation of FCRA 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) and 1681e ( b ) Accuracy and Reasonable Procedures XXXX  is reporting a balance that was paid in full by Texas Rent Relief and therefore no longer owed by me. Reporting a paid government-assisted rental balance as a consumer debt is materially inaccurate. XXXX  has failed to maintain reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy. 
2. Violation of FCRA 1681s-2 ( b ) Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Investigation I have disputed this account multiple times and informed XXXX  that the debt was satisfied through Texas Rent Relief XXXX XXXX  relied solely on automated verification from the furnisher without reviewing documentary evidence of payment or legal responsibility. This does not meet the standard of a reasonable investigation. 
3. Violation of FCRA 1681c ( a ) and 1681c ( b ) Improper Re-Reporting After Deletion XXXX  deleted this account after it could not be verified. XXXX  continues to re-report the account without providing the required certification of accuracy and completeness. If an account is deleted due to lack of verification, it may not be reinserted unless strict statutory requirements are met, including advance consumer notice. I did not receive any lawful reinsertion notice. 
4. Violation of FCRA 1681g ( a ) ( 1 ) Failure to Disclose Verification Method XXXX  has not disclosed the actual method used to verify ownership of this account, nor whether any documentary evidence was reviewed. Merely stating verified as accurate is insufficient when the debt has been paid by a government program and another bureau has deleted it. 
5. Legal Status of Texas Rent Relief Payments Texas Rent Relief payments satisfy rental obligations on behalf of tenants. Once payment is issued and accepted, the tenant is not legally bonded to the debt. Continuing to report the balance as consumer liability is inaccurate and misleading. 

Requested Resolution : Immediate permanent deletion of this account from my XXXX  credit report Written confirmation that the account will not be reinserted Correction of any internal records reflecting consumer liability for this debt XXXX continued reporting of a paid, unverified rental debt has caused ongoing harm and constitutes noncompliance with the FCRA. This complaint is submitted to request regulatory intervention and corrective action.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am a federal student loan borrower enrolled in the XXXX income-driven repayment plan, and I am submitting this complaint regarding the loss of qualifying payment credit due to involuntary administrative forbearance. 

According to my loan servicer, I have already made XXXX qualifying payments toward the required XXXX for forgiveness, leaving only XXXX payments remaining. 

This means I was nearing completion of my repayment term and approaching loan forgiveness after many years of consistent payments. 

However, due to ongoing legal challenges to the XXXX plan, my loans were placed into mandatory administrative forbearance. I did not request this forbearance and was not given the option to continue making qualifying payments under an income-driven repayment plan. 

My servicer has explicitly stated that : -I am required to remain in forbearance -Interest has resumed accruing -Time spent in forbearance does not count toward qualifying payments As a result, I lost critical progress toward forgiveness despite having made over XXXX qualifying payments. I was willing and able to continue making payments but was prevented from doing so due to government action. 

This situation is particularly harmful because I was so close to reaching forgiveness. Being forced into a non-qualifying status at this stage effectively delays or jeopardizes the completion of my repayment after more than a decade of compliance. 

Additionally, I have made multiple inquiries regarding my qualifying payment count and remaining balance, and accurate, timely information has been difficult to obtain, further compounding the issue. 

This situation creates a fundamental unfairness : -Borrowers are required to enter forbearance involuntarily -Borrowers are not allowed to make qualifying payments -Borrowers then lose credit toward forgiveness Borrowers should not be penalized for circumstances outside of their control, particularly when they are actively attempting to comply with repayment requirements. 

I am requesting that the Department of Education : Count months spent in XXXX-related administrative forbearance as qualifying payments toward forgiveness or provide a mechanism to receive retroactive credit for these months. 

This issue affects millions of borrowers and is especially harmful to those nearing forgiveness after many years of repayment. The current policy undermines the integrity of the repayment system and places an unfair burden on borrowers who have complied with all requirements.

Consumer complaint narrative:
To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding a collection account being reported by Contract Callers Inc. without legally sufficient proof that it owns, was assigned, or otherwise has authority to collect or report this alleged debt. 

Account Information Collection Agency : Contract Callers Inc. 

Account Number : XXXX Original Creditor : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Date Placed for Collection : XXXX XXXX XXXX  Amount Allegedly Owed : {$1100.00} Portfolio Type : Collection Current Status : Placed for Collection Last Verified Date : XX/XX/year> Failure to Produce Required Assignment Contracts Contract Callers Inc. is reporting this account as a collection obligation but has failed to provide competent, admissible proof of legal assignment or ownership of this debt. 

Under federal law, a third-party debt collector must be able to demonstrate a lawful chain of assignment from the original creditor to itself. This requires : A bill of sale, assignment agreement, or purchase contract Documentation that specifically identifies this consumers account Proof that Contract Callers Inc. has the legal authority to collect and furnish data to consumer reporting agencies A billing statement from the original creditor is NOT legally sufficient. 
Billing statements do not establish ownership, assignment, or authority, and anyone can create or reproduce such documents. Federal verification standards require assignment contracts, not generic account statements. 

Absent valid assignment documentation, Contract Callers Inc. has no permissible purpose to report this account.

Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Violations By continuing to report this collection without proof of legal assignment, Contract Callers Inc. is violating the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including but not limited to : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) Furnishing information that is inaccurate, incomplete, or materially misleading. 

15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation and verify legal authority after dispute.

15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to maintain reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy.

Reporting a collection account without proof of ownership is materially misleading and unlawful. 

Demand for Relief I hereby demand that Contract Callers Inc. : Immediately delete this tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies, including XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 

This complaint is being submitted to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) for regulatory review and enforcement. 

Please provide a written response within the CFPBs required response timeframe.

To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding an inaccurately and unlawfully reported collection account being furnished by Source Receivables Management. 

Account Information Collection Agency : Source Receivables Management Account Number : XXXX Original Creditor : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 

Date Placed for Collection : XX/XX/XXXX Amount Allegedly Owed : {$2100.00} Portfolio Type : Collection Current Status : Placed for Collection Last Verified Date : XX/XX/XXXX Failure to Provide Proof of Legal Assignment Source Receivables Management is reporting this account as a collection obligation without providing any admissible proof that it has the legal right to collect or report this debt. 

Under federal law, a third-party debt collector must be able to demonstrate a valid chain of assignment from the original creditor to itself. This includes : A bill of sale, assignment agreement, or purchase contract Documentation identifying this specific account as included in the transfer Proof that the collector has authority to collect and furnish data to consumer reporting agencies Merely sending a billing statement or screenshot from the original creditor is not legally sufficient. 
Anyone can generate or reproduce a bill such documents do not establish ownership or assignment. 

Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Violations Source Receivables Managements reporting violates multiple provisions of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) Furnishing information that is inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading.

15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation and verify ownership and authority upon dispute.

15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy. 

Without proof of a lawful assignment, Source Receivables Management has no permissible purpose to report this account. 

Demand for Relief I formally demand that Source Receivables Management : Immediately delete this tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies, including XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint regarding a medical debt that a collection agency has failed to properly validate after receiving my written dispute.

* A detailed, itemized billing statement from the original medical provider. 
* Proof that the amount claimed is accurate and includes no unauthorized fees or charges. 
* Documentation showing the collector has legal authority to collect this specific debt. 

Despite my timely dispute, the collector has continued collection efforts and/or reported this account to credit reporting agencies without first providing proper validation.

I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this matter and require the collector to : * Provide proper validation of the alleged medical debt. 
* Cease collection activity until validation is provided. 
* Correct or remove any inaccurate credit reporting associated with this account. 

I have attached copies of my validation request and relevant correspondence. 

Thank you for your assistance in resolving this matter. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX east XXXX XXXX XXXX, GA, XXXX

Despite this volume and pattern of credits, Citibank has alternated among Security Credit Issued, Customer Responsible ( No Credit Issued ), and Credit Reversed determinations on transactions sharing materially similar characteristics, without identifying transaction-specific evidentiary distinctions. This pattern raises concerns regarding the consistency of Citibanks application of Truth in Lending Act and Regulation Z billing error standards under 15 U.S.C. 1666 and 12 C.F.R. 1026.13. 

Illustrative Transaction Comparisons Example 1 : XXXX XXXX XXXX NY {$290.00} Disputed XX/XX/XXXX Security Credit Issued ( XX/XX/XXXX ) XXXX XXXX XXXX NY {$290.00} Disputed XX/XX/XXXX Customer Responsible ( No Credit Issued ) Example 2 : XXXX XXXX Coins {$44.00} Disputed XX/XX/XXXX Security Credit Issued Comparable merchant-family transactions Denied using identical boilerplate language. 

Applicable Law Under 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( a ), upon receipt of a billing error notice, a creditor must investigate and either correct the error or provide a written explanation clarifying why the charge is believed to be correct. Regulation Z requires : 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( b ) ( investigation of billing errors ) ; 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( e ) ( correction where error is found ) ; 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( f ) ( reasonable investigation and written explanation of results ) ; and 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( g ) ( restriction on collection of disputed amounts during investigation ). A written explanation must reflect the investigation actually conducted and identify the basis upon which the creditor concluded the transaction was authorized.

This demonstrates that merchant-provided materials were not treated as self-proving. This variability raises concerns regarding uniform application of investigative standards under 1026.13 ( f ).

The letters do not identify whether AVS results were reviewed, whether CVV verification was confirmed, whether IP/device consistency was analyzed, or what evidentiary distinction justified differing outcomes among materially similar transactions. Without articulated differentiation, the written explanation requirement of 1026.13 ( f ) is not meaningfully satisfied.

Recently we learned that the initial disbursement has been ( improperly ) reduced to approximately {$15000.00} based on the incorrect assumption that prior payments were issued to us. 

This is factually inaccurate. 

The payments in question were for water mitigation, mold remediation, lead mitigation and emergency services and were paid directly by the insurance carrier and/or disbursed by our public adjuster directly to vendors. Those funds were never issued to us, never endorsed by us, and never processed through your institution. 

Despite being informed of this distinction by both XXXX, our homeowner 's insurance company, and XXXX XXXX, our retained public adjuster, Freedom Mortgage 's loss processor continues to treat those third-party vendor payments as though they were borrower-controlled reconstruction funds. As a result, Freedom Mortgage is improperly reducing the reconstruction funds available to restore my home. 

The emergency abatement costs are separate and apart from the reconstruction costs. I have uploaded two separate reconstruction quotes to the Freedom Mortgage portal that supports the expense required to get my home to a livable state. The expenses that have been paid to vendors, which I have not ever received, were used to mitigate the vast amounts of water damage in my condo - sheetrock was crumbling, the floors were literal sponges, my downstairs neighbors two floors down were being impacted, mold was forming, my condo was a hazmat scene and needed emergency intervention. The funds used to pay those vendors were used to remove hazardous materials ( lead ) sheetrock and the floors. Our condo is sitting leveled down to the metal studs and concrete floors. We had severe water damage. ( photos provided ) Stage 1 - Mitigation- this was paid directly by our public adjuster and included cleanup of the water, mold, lead abatement, etc Stage 2 - Reconstruction- this is a separate process that needs to be paid out of the funds Freedom Mortgage is holding in escrow We have explained this several times, as have our insurance company and our public adjuster. 

This delay is materially impacting our ability to complete reconstruction and return our home to livable condition. We can not live in our condo and have not been able to do so since the damage was discovered on XX/XX/XXXX. 

Freedom Mortgage 's Loss Draft representative we spoke with on XX/XX/XXXX said Freedom Mortgage cares more about our home than XXXX, implying they are looking out for our best interest more than anyone else. I have repeatedly requested Freedom Mortgage show us that by issuing us the standard initial {$40000.00} draw so we can begin properly funding this construction project in a way that is not financially strapping my family. 

Freedom Mortgage has been in control of our reconstruction funds for 2 months. We now understand that our case is under review based on their Loss Draft Processor 's erroneous request to change the initial payment from {$40000.00} to {$15000.00} because they are wrongly applying prior payments made for water and lead abatement toward reconstruction costs. I am worried they will not review my case in its accurate totality. 

Freedom Mortgage is putting financial strain on my family by holding XXXX the funds that have been issued to cover the cost of reconstruction to my condo. Funds that have been made available through an insurance policy that I pay for. If they were to reduce our reconstruction budget by {$25000.00} ( I am basing this on their purported reduction of our initial draw from {$40000.00} to {$15000.00} ) I would not be able to move back into my condo - a home that I own together with Freedom Mortgage. The reason why is because that would not be enough to cover the cost of reconstruction. Also, what will Freedom Mortgage do with the {$25000.00} they are seemingly withholding? Will they keep it for themselves? I can not find any stipulation or clause in any contract that states they are allowed to keep these funds. 

Our reconstruction project is starting on Monday, XX/XX/XXXX. We were going to lose the ability to work with our very carefully selected vendor ( they have been waiting patiently for nearly 2 months ) if we did not get them on this project now. In addition, our primary residence has been uninhabitable since XX/XX/XXXX. 

We scheduled Freedom Mortgage 's inspector to come by last week on either XX/XX/XXXX or XX/XX/XXXX but we never received confirmation from him that he actually went there. We have called him several times and he has not returned our calls. It concerns me that Freedom Mortgage will use this as another reason to add a bottleneck to this process.

FORMAL NOTICE OF DISPUTE DEMAND FOR VALIDATION, PROOF OF OWNERSHIP, AND PROOF OF STANDING To Whom It May Concern : This letter serves as a formal dispute of the above-referenced account. I recently discovered that Jefferson Capital Systems , LLC is reporting this alleged debt on my consumer credit reports.

I have never received the required written notice within five ( 5 ) days of your initial communication, as required under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( a ) of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ). Your failure to provide the mandatory notice is a violation of federal law.

This alleged debt is hereby disputed in its entirety.

DEMAND FOR VALIDATION ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ) Pursuant to the FDCPA and applicable case law, you are required to cease collection activity and reporting until you provide proper validation.

In order to validate this debt, you must provide : The name and address of the original creditor The amount of the alleged debt, with a full accounting The date of default The date of charge-off A complete payment history The contract bearing my signature DEMAND FOR PROOF OF OWNERSHIP AND STANDING Because Jefferson Capital is not the original creditor, you must also prove you have lawful ownership and standing to collect and report this alleged debt.

You are required to produce : The Purchase and Sale Agreement The Forward Flow Agreement The Bill of Sale The specific Account-Level Assignment showing my account number The complete Chain of Title from the original creditor to Jefferson Capital Any assignment contract evidencing transfer of rights Courts have consistently held that a debt buyer must prove standing and ownership through competent evidence. 

In XXXX v. Portfolio Recovery Associates, the Court held that a debt buyer must demonstrate actual ownership and assignment of the specific account in order to establish standing.

Generalized bills of sale without account-level identification are insufficient.

NOTICE REGARDING CREDIT REPORTING If you continue to report this account without proper validation and proof of ownership, you may be in violation of : 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( false representation ) 15 U.S.C. 1692f ( unfair practices ) 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) ( continuing collection without validation ) 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) ( failure to conduct reasonable investigation ) Continued reporting without proof of ownership may constitute furnishing information you can not substantiate.

DEMAND FOR DELETION If you can not provide the above documentation within 30 days, you must : Immediately cease collection activity Delete all credit reporting related to this account Provide written confirmation of deletion NOTICE OF INTENT TO ESCALATE If Jefferson Capital fails to comply, I reserve all rights to : Initiate arbitration pursuant to any governing agreement File suit in Federal Court Seek statutory damages under the FDCPA Seek actual damages and attorneys fees Seek damages under the FCRA This letter is not a refusal to pay, but a notice that your claim is disputed and must be validated.

Govern yourselves accordingly.

Consumer complaint narrative:
On a prior dispute, these student loan accounts were removed from my credit report after being identified as identity theft. Subsequently, the accounts were reinserted onto my report with different start dates and different loan amounts. 

I was not provided advance written notice of reinsertion as required under 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ) ( ii ). Additionally, because these accounts were previously disputed as identity theft, reinsertion without proper certification of accuracy and compliance with 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 raises concerns regarding unlawful re-reporting of identity theft information. 

The reinserted tradelines contain materially different account details, including modified dates and balances, which suggests inaccurate or inconsistent reporting. 

I request documentation showing : Certification of accuracy used to justify reinsertion Written notice of reinsertion sent to me Documentation linking me to the account Method of verification used prior to reinsertion If the furnisher and credit reporting agency can not demonstrate full compliance with FCRA reinsertion requirements, the accounts must be permanently deleted. 


Now for What would be a fair resolution? paste this : A fair resolution would be permanent deletion of the reinserted student loan accounts unless the company can provide documented certification of accuracy and proof of compliance with 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ) and 1681c-2. 

In addition to the student loan reinsertion issue, I am disputing inaccurate reporting related to a vehicle repossession account. 

The tradeline reflects repossession and/or collection-related derogatory coding ; however, I requested documentation substantiating the reporting, including the Date of First Delinquency, date of repossession, date of sale, itemized deficiency balance calculation, and documentation supporting any collection placement. 

No such documentation has been provided. 

Under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), a furnisher must conduct a reasonable investigation after receiving notice of dispute and must correct or delete information that can not be verified. Under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), reporting must reflect maximum possible accuracy and must not be materially misleading. 

If the account is being reported simultaneously as a repossession, charge-off, and/or collection without clear and accurate status coding and supporting documentation, such reporting may create a materially misleading credit impression. 

Because the furnisher has failed to provide documentary substantiation and continues furnishing derogatory information with disputed status coding, I request correction or deletion consistent with FCRA requirements. 

Now for Fair resolution you can strengthen it like this : A fair resolution would be permanent deletion of the reinserted student loan accounts and correction or deletion of the repossession tradeline unless the company can provide documented certification of accuracy and proof of compliance with 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ), 1681c-2, 1681e ( b ), and 1681s-2 ( b ).

FORMAL NOTICE OF DISPUTE DEMAND FOR VALIDATION, PROOF OF OWNERSHIP, AND PROOF OF STANDING To Whom It May Concern : This letter serves as a formal dispute of the above-referenced account. I recently discovered that Jefferson Capital Systems , LLC is reporting this alleged debt on my consumer credit reports. 

I have never received the required written notice within five ( 5 ) days of your initial communication, as required under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( a ) of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ). Your failure to provide the mandatory notice is a violation of federal law. 

This alleged debt is hereby disputed in its entirety. 

DEMAND FOR VALIDATION ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ) Pursuant to the FDCPA and applicable case law, you are required to cease collection activity and reporting until you provide proper validation. 

In order to validate this debt, you must provide : The name and address of the original creditor The amount of the alleged debt, with a full accounting The date of default The date of charge-off A complete payment history The contract bearing my signature DEMAND FOR PROOF OF OWNERSHIP AND STANDING Because XXXX XXXX XXXX not the original creditor, you must also prove you have lawful ownership and standing to collect and report this alleged debt. 

You are required to produce : The Purchase and Sale Agreement The Forward Flow Agreement The Bill of Sale The specific Account-Level Assignment showing my account number The complete Chain of Title from the original creditor to XXXX XXXX Any assignment contract evidencing transfer of rights Courts have consistently held that a debt buyer must prove standing and ownership through competent evidence. 

In XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, the Court held that a debt buyer must demonstrate actual ownership and assignment of the specific account in order to establish standing. 

Generalized bills of sale without account-level identification are insufficient. 

NOTICE REGARDING CREDIT REPORTING If you continue to report this account without proper validation and proof of ownership, you may be in violation of : 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( false representation ) 15 U.S.C. 1692f ( unfair practices ) 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) ( continuing collection without validation ) 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) ( failure to conduct reasonable investigation ) Continued reporting without proof of ownership may constitute furnishing information you can not substantiate. 

DEMAND FOR DELETION If you can not provide the above documentation within 30 days, you must : Immediately cease collection activity Delete all credit reporting related to this account Provide written confirmation of deletion NOTICE OF INTENT TO ESCALATE If Jefferson Capital fails to comply, I reserve all rights to : Initiate arbitration pursuant to any governing agreement File suit in Federal Court Seek statutory damages under the FDCPA Seek actual damages and attorneys fees Seek damages under the FCRA This letter is not a refusal to pay, but a notice that your claim is disputed and must be validated. 

Govern yourselves accordingly.

TO : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Primary Originator/Seller ) [ XXXX  Address from your records ] AND MOHELA ( Missouri Higher Education Loan Authority ) ( Current Servicer ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  XXXX XXXX : FINAL NOTICE OF DISPUTE / DEMAND FOR FULL VALIDATION PURSUANT TO 15 U.S.C. 1692g Account Number ( s ) : [ Your Account # XXXX ] CIP/Batch ID ( if known ) : [ Look for any identifiers on old statements ] CUSIP Request : Pending Validation To the General Counsels of XXXX  and MOHELA : I am writing to formally dispute the validity of the debt referenced above. This letter serves as a continuation of my complaint filed with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) and addresses the insufficient response provided by XXXX  on XX/XX/year>, which attempted to redirect this matter to MOHELA. 

Your attempt to close my complaint by stating the loan was " transferred '' is procedurally improper and substantively deficient. A transfer of servicing does not extinguish the originator 's liability regarding the chain of title, nor does it satisfy the legal requirement for debt validation. 
1. Jurisdictional and Standing Arguments The " Transfer '' Defense is Invalid. 
XXXX, you originated this debt. As confirmed by recent SEC filings and your own corporate disclosures, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX acts as the " Master Servicer and Administrator '' for various XXXX  Student Loan Trusts, while XXXX  XXXX, XXXX acts as the " Depositor ''. Even though MOHELA now handles the day-to-day servicing, XXXX  retains ownership and control over the economic terms of the loans. The agreement between XXXX  and MOHELA explicitly states that MOHELA has not purchased the loans ; XXXX  has merely outsourced the administrative functions. 

MOHELA, as the current servicer, you are not immune to this dispute. You are now the face of this debt. If XXXX  can not prove the chain of title and that this debt was lawfully assigned to a trust, you are servicing an invalid instrument. 
2. Demand for Full Validation ( Chain of Title & Securitization ) Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and Regulation F ( 12 CFR 1006.34 ), validation requires more than a statement of the balance. It requires proof that the entity collecting has the legal right to do so. Copies of old Master Promissory Notes ( MPNs ) are insufficient. 

To validate this debt, I demand the production of the following specific documents within 15 days : The Indenture and Sale Agreement : If this loan was securitized, it was conveyed via a Sale Agreement to a Trust. I demand a copy of the relevant Indenture ( similar to the XXXX Student Loan Trust XXXX or XXXX indentures on file with the SEC ). 

Identification of the Trustee : Provide the name and contact information for the Indenture Trustee ( e.g., XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) and the Eligible Lender Trustee who holds legal title to the loans. 

CUSIP Number : Provide the CUSIP number for the specific Note ( tranche ) that allegedly contains my loan. If my loan was pooled into a security, it has a CUSIP. Failure to provide this suggests the debt is not held in the manner required by law. 

Chain of Title Flow : Provide a transactional history showing the path of the debt from origination ( XXXX  ) to the Depositor ( XXXX XXXX ) to the Trust, and finally to the current holder. 

If the loan was not securitized, provide a notarized affidavit from a corporate officer stating that the debt remains on XXXX  's balance sheet and has not been sold, nor the economic interest transferred. 
3. The Consequence of Non-Validation : XXXX Balance and Deletion Required If XXXX  and MOHELA can not produce the documentation demanded abovespecifically the chain of title, the trust documents, and the CUSIPit is an admission that the debt is not real and can not be enforced. 

A debt that can not be validated is a nullity. It has no legal standing. Therefore, if you fail to provide these documents, you are hereby on notice that : You must immediately instruct all credit reporting agencies ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) to delete the trade lines associated with this account. A " XXXX balance '' is insufficient ; the entire entry must be removed because it was never proven valid. 

You must cease all collection activities permanently. 

You must cease all reporting activities permanently. 

By failing to provide the validation documents requested, you are implicitly admitting that the debt is unenforceable and that any reporting of this debt on my credit file constitutes a fraudulent misrepresentation under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 
4. The D.O.G.E. Data Glitch and Inaccurate Reporting XXXX  's reliance on corrupted dataspecifically the " D.O.G.E. '' systemic glitchrenders any accounting provided thus far presumptively inaccurate. You have a duty to ensure data integrity before transferring accounts to MOHELA or reporting to credit bureaus. 

Furthermore, XXXX  was recently ordered to pay {$120.00} XXXX to settle claims of loan mismanagement with the CFPB and was banned from servicing federal student loans. Given this history of non-compliance, I have no reason to trust that the data transferred to MOHELA is accurate. I demand a " life of loan '' accounting from XXXX  that reconciles every penny from origination to transfer. 
5. Human Rights Framework ( UDHR & ICESCR ) Beyond statutory law, this dispute touches upon fundamental human rights. 

UDHR Article 26 and ICESCR Article 13 establish that higher education shall be made equally accessible to all on the basis of capacity. 

The securitization and speculative trading of student loan debt transforms a social goodeducationinto a commodity. When the chain of title is broken, or when debts are validated based on corrupted data, it creates a clouded title on a human right. 

You can not claim the protections of commerce ( selling the debt as a security ) while ignoring the burdens of proof required by law. I demand that you prove you have clear title to this debt, otherwise your collection efforts constitute an unjust enrichment derived from the obstruction of my right to education. 

6. Data Privacy and Sale of Information XXXX, there are also allegations and concerns regarding the sale or transfer of borrower information. The transfer of servicing to MOHELA does not grant an automatic right to the endless sharing of my private financial data without explicit, renewed consent. I demand an accounting of what specific data points were transferred and which third-party data brokers or investors have received access to my file. 

Conclusion and Demands To be clear, copies of statements do not validate a debt. To close this matter, I demand the following : From XXXX  : The full securitization audit trail, including the name of the Indenture Trustee, the Pooling and Servicing Agreement ( or Indenture ), and the specific CUSIP for the trust containing my loan. 

From XXXX  : A verification that the data transferred to MOHELA was scrubbed of the " D.O.G.E. '' glitch errors, or a correction of the record if it was not. 

From MOHELA : A freeze on all collection and credit reporting activities until XXXX  provides the validation demanded above. 

From Both : If the validation documents are not produced within 15 days of receipt of this letter, you must immediately delete all trade lines associated with this account from my credit reports and provide written confirmation of such deletions. Your failure to validate constitutes your admission that the debt is not real and can not be enforced. 

Until these documents are produced, the debt is disputed, and the validity is unproven. Continued collection or reporting on an unvalidated debt will be met with further legal action, including complaints to the FTC regarding pattern and practice violations and a suit for damages under the FDCPA. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX Without Prejudice | UCC 1-308

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am submitting this complaint regarding inaccurate, unfair, and improperly reported delinquencies by Nelnet related to my federal student loans during the repayment restart and administrative transition period following the federal XXXX payment pause. 

Nelnet reported my account as delinquent for XXXX and XX/XX/year>, despite the fact that these months fell during a period of widespread, well-documented servicing disruptions associated with the federal repayment restart. During this transition, borrowers were moving from the payment pause into repayment, XXXX  eligibility, or administrative forbearance, and servicers were required to ensure accurate account coding and adequate borrower notice. 

Nelnet failed to provide clear, timely, and adequate notice that my account had entered active repayment or that payments were due for the months reported as late. I did not receive sufficient communication establishing that repayment had properly resumed or that failure to pay would be reported as delinquency. As a result, my account should not have been reported as past due during this transition period. 

Further, Nelnet failed to apply appropriate administrative forbearance during the repayment restart, despite widespread acknowledgment by the Department of Education and the CFPB that many accounts were mis-coded or improperly placed into repayment during this period. I raised this issue directly with Nelnet, yet Nelnet denied my request without providing documentation demonstrating proper notice, accurate repayment status, or justification for reporting these months as delinquent rather than administratively forborne. 

Additionally, the educational institution associated with these loans is now closed, which raises further concerns regarding the validity of ongoing servicing, repayment status determinations, and whether these loans were properly administered and reported during the transition period. 

During the period in question, I was also incarcerated, which further limited my ability to receive, access, or respond to communications regarding any alleged repayment obligations during the federal repayment restart. This circumstance made clear, timely, and accurate notice from Nelnet especially critical, yet no such notice was received. This further demonstrates that any reported delinquency was not willful, and that Nelnet failed to exercise reasonable care in servicing and reporting my account during the administrative transition. 

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 ), furnishers of information must ensure that credit reporting is accurate, verifiable, complete, and not misleading. Reporting delinquency during a period when administrative forbearance should have applied, where notice was deficient, and where borrower capacity was impaired, constitutes inaccurate and unfair credit reporting.

Nelnet has failed to provide : Proof of proper repayment notice, Evidence of correct account coding during the repayment restart, Or documentation substantiating that these months were legitimately due and delinquent.

Requested Resolution I respectfully request that Nelnet : 1. Correct or delete the XXXX XXXX  late payment reporting ; XXXX. Apply retroactive administrative forbearance for the affected months ; XXXX. Update all credit bureaus ( XXXX XXXX and XXXX  ) to reflect accurate reporting ; XXXX. Provide written documentation explaining how Nelnet determined these payments were due during the transition period and how notice was allegedly provided. 

If Nelnet can not fully substantiate the accuracy of this reporting with proper documentation, the negative credit information must be removed.

TO : XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( Primary Originator/Seller ) [ XXXX Address from your records ] AND MOHELA ( Missouri Higher Education Loan Authority ) ( Current Servicer ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX MO XXXX XXXX : FINAL NOTICE OF DISPUTE / DEMAND FOR FULL VALIDATION PURSUANT TO 15 U.S.C. 1692g Account Number ( s ) : [ Your Account XXXX XXXXXXXX ] CIP/Batch ID ( if known ) : [ Look for any identifiers on old statements ] CUSIP Request : Pending Validation To the General Counsels of XXXX and MOHELA : I am writing to formally dispute the validity of the debt referenced above. This letter serves as a continuation of my complaint filed with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) and addresses the insufficient response provided by Navient on XX/XX/year>, which attempted to redirect this matter to MOHELA. 

Your attempt to close my complaint by stating the loan was " transferred '' is procedurally improper and substantively deficient. A transfer of servicing does not extinguish the originator 's liability regarding the chain of title, nor does it satisfy the legal requirement for debt validation. 
1. Jurisdictional and Standing Arguments The " Transfer '' Defense is Invalid. 
XXXX, you originated this debt. As confirmed by recent SEC filings and your own corporate disclosures, XXXX XXXX, XXXX acts as the " Master Servicer and XXXX '' for various SLM Student Loan Trusts, while XXXX XXXX, XXXX acts as the " Depositor ''. Even though MOHELA now handles the day-to-day servicing, XXXX retains ownership and XXXX over the economic terms of the loans. The agreement between XXXX and MOHELA explicitly states that MOHELA has not purchased the loans ; XXXX has merely outsourced the administrative functions. 

MOHELA, as the current servicer, you are not immune to this dispute. You are now the face of this debt. If XXXX can not prove the chain of title and that this debt was lawfully assigned to a trust, you are servicing an invalid instrument. 
XXXX. Demand for Full Validation ( Chain of XXXX & Securitization ) Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and Regulation F ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ), validation requires more than a statement of the balance. It requires proof that the entity collecting has the legal right to do so. Copies of old XXXX XXXX XXXX ( MPNs ) are insufficient. 

To validate this debt, I demand the production of the following specific documents within 15 days : The Indenture and Sale Agreement : If this loan was securitized, it was conveyed via a Sale Agreement to a Trust. I demand a copy of the relevant Indenture ( similar to the XXXX Student Loan Trust XXXX or XXXX indentures on file with the SEC ). 

Identification of the Trustee : Provide the name and contact information for the Indenture Trustee ( e.g., XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) and the Eligible Lender Trustee who holds legal title to the loans. 

XXXX XXXX : Provide the CUSIP number for the specific Note ( tranche ) that allegedly contains my loan. If my loan was pooled into a security, it has a CUSIP. Failure to provide this suggests the debt is not held in the manner required by law. 

Chain of Title Flow : Provide a transactional history showing the path of the debt from origination ( Navient ) to the Depositor ( XXXX Funding ) to the Trust, and finally to the current holder. 

If the loan was not securitized, provide a notarized affidavit from a corporate XXXX stating that the debt remains on XXXX 's balance sheet and has not been sold, nor the economic interest transferred. 
XXXX. The Consequence of Non-Validation : XXXX Balance and Deletion Required If XXXX and MOHELA can not produce the documentation demanded abovespecifically the chain of title, the trust documents, and the XXXX is an admission that the debt is not real and can not be enforced. 

A debt that can not be validated is a nullity. It has no legal standing. Therefore, if you fail to provide these documents, you are hereby on notice that : You must immediately instruct all credit reporting agencies ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) to delete the trade lines associated with this account. A " XXXX balance '' is insufficient ; the entire entry must be removed because it was never proven valid. 

You must cease all collection activities permanently. 

You must cease all reporting activities permanently. 

By failing to provide the validation documents requested, you are implicitly admitting that the debt is unenforceable and that any reporting of this debt on my credit file constitutes a fraudulent misrepresentation under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 
4. The D.O.G.E. Data Glitch and Inaccurate Reporting Navient 's reliance on corrupted dataspecifically the " D.O.G.E. '' systemic glitchrenders any accounting provided thus far presumptively inaccurate. You have a duty to ensure data integrity before transferring accounts to MOHELA or reporting to credit bureaus. 

Furthermore, XXXX was recently ordered to pay {$120.00} XXXX to settle claims of loan mismanagement with the CFPB and was banned from servicing federal student loans. Given this history of non-compliance, I have no reason to trust that the data transferred to MOHELA is accurate. I demand a " life of loan '' accounting from XXXX that reconciles every XXXX from origination to transfer. 
XXXX. XXXX Rights XXXX ( XXXX & XXXX ) XXXX statutory law, this dispute touches upon fundamental human rights. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX establish that higher education shall be made equally accessible to all on the basis of capacity. 

The securitization and speculative trading of student loan debt transforms a social goodeducationinto a commodity. When the chain of title is broken, or when debts are validated based on corrupted data, it creates a clouded title on a human right. 

You can not claim the protections of commerce ( selling the debt as a security ) while ignoring the burdens of proof required by law. I demand that you prove you have clear title to this debt, otherwise your collection efforts constitute an unjust enrichment derived from the obstruction of my right to education. 

XXXX. Data Privacy and Sale of XXXX XXXX, there are also allegations and concerns regarding the sale or transfer of borrower information. The transfer of servicing to MOHELA does not XXXX an automatic right to the endless sharing of my private financial data without explicit, renewed consent. I demand an accounting of what specific data points were transferred and which third-party data brokers or investors have received access to my file. 

Conclusion and Demands To be clear, copies of statements do not validate a debt. To close this matter, I demand the following : From XXXX : The full securitization XXXX XXXX, including the name of the Indenture Trustee, the Pooling and Servicing Agreement ( or Indenture ), and the specific CUSIP for the trust containing my loan. 

From XXXX : A verification that the data transferred to MOHELA was scrubbed of the " D.O.G.E. '' glitch errors, or a correction of the record if it was not. 

From MOHELA : A freeze on all collection and credit reporting activities until XXXX provides the validation demanded above. 

From Both : If the validation documents are not produced within 15 days of receipt of this letter, you must immediately delete all trade lines associated with this account from my credit reports and provide written confirmation of such deletions. Your failure to validate constitutes your admission that the debt is not real and can not be enforced. 

Until these documents are produced, the debt is disputed, and the validity is unproven. Continued collection or reporting on an unvalidated debt will be met with further legal action, including complaints to the FTC regarding pattern and practice violations and a suit for damages under the FDCPA. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX Without Prejudice | XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative:
SCHWARTZ VAYS Schwartz Vays has been predatory and abusive of its position as a debt collector in its dealings with me. This company is very, very efficient at sending email and letters in the post under the guise of wanting to work with me but it has in fact made no effort at all to resolve the debt issue. Truthfully, they have behaved in exactly the opposite manner once I contacted them on Friday XX/XX/XXXX and onwards. They have dropped the ball at every turn and are not taking any responsibility for the reality that they are 100 % the reason why we have not entered in an agreement to resolve the debt. I do not deny that I owe debt but I vehemently dispute I owe anything beyond what I owed effective Monday XX/XX/XXXX. Let me explain. 

Schwartz Vays was contracted by the management company of my XXXX properties to collect the outstanding HOA fees. 

Friday XX/XX/XXXX - I called Schwartz Vays to work on securing a payment plan. I spoke with a Customer Rep., XXXX. We spoke about the XXXX property, xxx XXXX XXXX. She gave me the following details which were relevant : the outstanding amount was {$1500.00} which included the unpaid amount as well as the future assessment of {$480.00} assessment for XX/XX/XXXX. 

XXXX offered me 3 monthly plan choices : a XXXX plan for {$710.00}, a XXXX plan for {$360.00} or a XXXX plan for {$240.00}. I chose the XXXX plan. I agreed to provide my bank account information and start the XXXX payment withdrawal on Monday XX/XX/XXXX and every month thereafter on the XXXX, with a 3-business-day reminder each month before the withdrawal. She explained that last collection from my bank account would be XX/XX/XXXX, at which point my debt would be fulfilled. XXXX said she would email me the contract with the aforementioned information : the amount outstanding through XX/XX/XXXX, the XXXX payment plan choice, the monthly payment amount and the length of the contract. 

XXXX was to give me an agreement on the same day, F XX/XX/XXXX, for the XXXX property once we got the XXXX property, XXXX, squared away. Unfortunately, the XXXX property never came into the scope because she was unable to provide me with a signable agreement for the XXXX property. 

This is where things went downhill. XXXX emailed me a contract for XXXX that only had the generic consent information ( see attached ). None of the information we spoke about was in it. None. XXXX sent the contract multiple times but the contract had nothing I could sign. She said she would try again on Monday XX/XX/XXXX. 

Monday XX/XX/XXXX- She called at XXXX XXXX  EST as a follow-up to Fridays conversation. The agreement sent still did not reflect the plan details. She said she would send the document from someone else 's computer to see if the document would then reflect the details. I received no further communication from her. 

Tuesday XX/XX/XXXX- I emailed Schwartz Vays summarizing my interaction with XXXX, indicating that I was expecting but had neither received any follow-up communication from XXXX nor a contract that I could sign. No response. 

Thursday XX/XX/XXXX - I sent a follow-up email to Schwartz Vays . No response. 

Monday XX/XX/XXXX- I received an email response from the Lead Customer Service Rep., XXXX XXXX, who stated that the agent, XXXX, had attempted to reach me on Thursday XX/XX/XXXX. 

Monday XX/XX/XXXX- I disputed that XXXX or anyone from Schwartz Vays had called me on Thursday XX/XX/XXXX since I did not have a log of the call. My contention is that if Schwartz Vays had been so eager to resolve the debt with me and XXXX was supposed to get me a signable contract on Friday XX/XX/XXXX, why did she drag her feet and allegedly contact me 5 business days later through a phantom phone call for which I do not have a record? 

I am the one who made the effort to resolve the issue during this time period, not Schwartz Vays. Instead of XXXX XXXX telling me to call the company again, she should have ensured a proper contract was sent to me. This company does not actually do anything but pose, posture and blow hot air. They were unable to provide a simple signable agreement, the very thing that is at the heart of the 'service ' it is supposed to provide. They have taken no responsibility for this inability to provide me with a signable contract. 

Monday XX/XX/XXXX - Instead, I got an email from XXXX XXXX regurgitating that I owed HOA fees on my XXXX properties, with no reference to getting me a contract but the usual dismissive solution to call them. From Monday XX/XX/XXXX through today, Wednesday XX/XX/XXXX, I have not received a single phone call from Schwartz Vays, which clearly demonstrates they had no real interest in resolving the debt. 

Thursday XX/XX/XXXX- I called Schwartz Vays and spoke with a Customer Rep, XXXX, I believe it was. She stated that I now owed over {$2100.00}, a lien was placed on my properties and I now had to put down 25 % because I broke the agreement I had established with the company. I explained to her that I had not broken an agreement because I had never received an agreement I could sign. I disagreed that I owed @ {$2100.00} inclusive of an additional {$200.00} fee Schwartz Vays had slapped on my account, and I stated that Schwartz Vays was culpable because it had not provided me a legal document that I could sign as was its legal responsibility to do. I requested that the lien be removed from my properties and the original agreement terms be offered to me which included the XXXX plan. 

XXXX explained that on Friday XX/XX/XXXX and the following week when I had engaged in communication with Schwartz Vays, their system was not working properly which is why they had been unable to provide me with a signable contract. I pointed out that since the breakdown and reason I had not signed a contract was entirely Schwartz Vays ' fault, they were and are culpable for the lack of a contract. They should bear responsibility for their malfunctioning system but they have not. It is unconscionable that they have taken no responsibility for the lack of a contract. She said my points were valid and she would have her manager call me the next day. 

Friday XX/XX/XXXX - I received no promised phone call from Schwartz Vays, either from the manager or from the representative I had spoken with the day before. 

Friday XX/XX/XXXX - I placed a follow up call on this date. I was told that the manager, XXXX, had been out of the office on F XX/XX/XXXX and was also out on this day, XX/XX/XXXX, but would be in the following day, XX/XX/XXXX, and would call me. I pointed out that there had been 5 business days between XX/XX/XXXX & XX/XX/XXXX during which he had had more than enough opportunity to call. 

Saturday XX/XX/XXXX - I received no promised phone call from the manager, XXXX, or from anyone from within Schwartz Vays. 

Wednesday XX/XX/XXXX- I have not received any answers to my missing contract. Please note that the only solution Schwartz Vays has ever offered once I engaged in communication with them is for me to call. Yet the calls achieve nothing. There is never any follow-up, no returned phone calls, and no email correspondence that addresses my issue. The ONLY thing this company has done is send the usual threatening emails and letters but they do nothing else. 

At this point, I have had no choice but to report Schwartz Vays to the CFPB. This company is operating in a nefarious and unethical manner and is not executing its contractual obligation to the HOA company which is to collect the outstanding HOA fees from its customers. 

Schwartz Vays has not provided me with a signable contract but an empty contract devoid of any of the terms of agreement initially sorted out on XX/XX/XXXX. 

Schwartz Vays has placed a lien on my properties even though they are culpable for there being no agreement. 

Schwartz Vays ' customer service has been negligent in its communication with me, have not returned phone calls they said would, and have provided no measurable solution although they have it documented in their database what the problem is and have a record of our conversations. 

Schwartz Vays ' only tactic is to harass, intimidate and exercise psychological warfare but not solve or resolve anything. I would appreciate if CFPB could report Schwartz Vays to the other governing bodies as someone should really investigate and do a deep dive into this company. They should not be allowed to stay in business with impunity. I doubt I am the only one who finds they are skirting the rules of fair and compliance of handling debt.

The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S. Code 1681 ) says ( 1 ) The banking system is dependent upon fair and accurate credit reporting. This is a violation of my privacy with my consumer report, since I control what is listed and what is not. In the event that any accounts are reported without my written consent, that is considered identity theft.

This is a violation of both 15 U.S. Code 1681b ( 2 ) and 15 U.S. Code 1681c-2. This leads way to civil liability against the credit reporting agency for negligent and willful noncompliance under 15 U.S. Code 1681n, which allows for {$1000.00} per violation, for account listed without my expressed written consent.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am disputing a recurring 'VIP program ' membership charge that I never authorized or knowingly enrolled in. While I did purchase medication from the merchant, I was never presented withnor did I agree toa separate paid membership.

I have made a good faith effort to resolve this with Discover Bank ( see my letter to them below ), but they have failed to conduct any reasonable investigation under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ). Their letter states simply " After considering all information you provided, we're unable to change the outcome of your dispute. Your dispute is resolved. and the transaction is valid. '' Instead of requiring the merchant to provide proof that I enrolled, Discover has issued a blanket denial and is now threatening to report this disputed amount to XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX. 

This practice of 'negative option ' enrollment ( charging for a service unless a consumer opts out of something they didn't know they were in ) is deceptive. I am requesting that Discover : Remove all charges related to this unauthorized program. 

Cease all negative reporting to credit bureaus regarding this disputed amount Date : XX/XX/XXXX Account Number : XXXX Total Disputed Amount : {$170.00} To the Discover Resolution Department, This letter serves as my formal and final notification regarding the disputed charges from " XXXX  XXXX '' totaling {$170.00}. I have closed my Discover account and paid my balance in full, excluding the aforementioned amount, which I will not be paying. 
I am withholding payment based on the following facts : Unauthorized Enrollment : In XX/XX/XXXX, I made a one-time purchase for dog medication ( {$120.00} ). I never authorized, requested, or signed up for a " VIP service. '' Merchant Bad Faith : When I discovered the {$29.00} monthly charges in XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted the merchant. The agent refused a refund and hung up when asked for identification. 
Fraudulent Claims by Merchant : XXXX XXXX  claimed to you that I never contacted them and that they attempted to reach me. I provided Discover with a phone log providing a XXXX call to them, which directly refutes their statement. 
Lack of Evidence : Discover has accepted a " refund policy '' as proof of a valid transaction. A refund policy is not a contract of enrollment. Discover has failed to produce a signed agreement or a recorded verification of my consent to this subscription. 
XXXX XXXX is a known predatory actor. Public consumer reports and forums ( such as XXXX and XXXX  Scam Tracker ) reveal a consistent pattern of 'Negative Option Billing ' by this merchant. Numerous other pet owners have reported being automatically enrolled in this exact {$29.00} 'VIP service ' without clear disclosure or consent. 
By siding with a merchant that has a public history of deceptive enrollment and proven false statements, Discover is failing its duty under the Fair Credit Billing Act to conduct a reasonable investigation into unauthorized charges. 
I have contacted Discover several times concerning this matter without fair resolution. I provided evidence in uploaded documents in the course of my dispute ( order receipts and phone log ) to disprove the merchants lies, yet Discover chose to side with a predatory billing practice. 
I understand that my decision to not pay for the {$170.00} XXXX XXXX  charged me may result in this balance being sent to a collection agency or impacting my credit score. Given the principle of this matter and Discovers failure to protect me from documented unauthorized billing, I am willing to accept that outcome. I will not be bullied into paying for a service I did not request/authorize. I will additionally file a complaint with the Consumer Finance Protection Bureau at the appropriate time.

Do not contact me further regarding the " validity '' of these charges unless you have a signed enrollment form from the merchant. 
Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX Discover already has uploaded documents, but they don't matter. The Merchant has to provide evidence that I ordered their subscription.

I am submitting this complaint regarding inaccurate and incomplete reporting of my federal student loan accounts by Equifax, Experian , and TransUnion.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am not disputing that I rented from XXXX XXXX XXXX. I am not asserting identity theft or fraud. I am disputing the accuracy, completeness, and substantiation of the {$1000.00} rental debt that XXXX XXXX XXXX is attempting to collect and furnish on behalf of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

I have documentary proof of five cashiers checks paid directly to XXXX XXXX XXXX totaling {$3100.00} : check XXXX for {$1100.00} dated XX/XX/XXXX, check XXXX for {$300.00} dated XX/XX/XXXX, check XXXX for {$170.00} dated XX/XX/XXXX, check XXXX for {$1100.00} dated XX/XX/XXXX, and check XXXX for {$350.00} dated XX/XX/XXXX. Three of the XX/XX/XXXX check numbers match the ledger payment references exactly : XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX. 

The ledger used to support the debt contains facial arithmetic defects. A balance of {$2800.00} plus a {$300.00} late charge should equal {$3100.00}, but the ledger shows {$3000.00}. Then {$3000.00} minus {$170.00} should equal {$2800.00}, but the ledger shows {$2700.00}. Then {$2700.00} minus {$1100.00} should equal {$1500.00}, but the ledger shows {$1800.00}. These are not minor clerical issues. They are objective running-balance errors that make the accounting unreliable on its face. 

The ledger also includes charges requiring exact support, including a {$300.00} late charge, {$310.00} XXXX late fees, {$50.00} XXXX late fee, and legal charges of {$38.00} and {$200.00}. The lease may allow certain categories of charges, but that does not prove these specific amounts were correctly calculated, properly applied, and accurately reported. The company must show the exact calculation, date basis, and contractual authority for each charge. 

The lease also reflects a {$1100.00} security deposit. If any part of the claimed balance depends on move-out charges, damage charges, cleaning charges, offsets, credits, or deposit application, then a full itemized accounting and supporting records should be produced. 

I also did not receive any initial written validation notice from XXXX XXXX XXXX before first learning of this alleged debt through my credit report. If notice was sent, the company should provide the date sent, address used, and a copy of the actual notice. 

Because the claimed {$1000.00} balance relies on an internally inconsistent ledger and incomplete substantiation, it is not reasonably verifiable as reported.

Subject : Follow-Up Complaint Regarding Continued Reporting of Mortgage Foreclosure ( Round 2 ) I am submitting this follow-up complaint regarding a mortgage account reported by Vanderbilt Mortgage that continues to appear on my credit report despite the foreclosure process being fully completed.

At the time this mortgage account became delinquent, I was experiencing significant financial hardship due to a divorce, which contributed to the circumstances surrounding the foreclosure. While I acknowledge the financial challenges, this does not excuse the inaccurate or misleading reporting of an account that has already been foreclosed.

Under 15 U.S.C. 6802 ( b ) of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, a financial institution may not disclose nonpublic personal financial information to nonaffiliated third parties without proper notice and an opportunity for the consumer to opt out. I am requesting documentation demonstrating that my financial information related to this mortgage account was furnished to credit reporting agencies in full compliance with 15 U.S.C. 6802 ( b ).

Additionally, under the Fair Credit Reporting Act : - 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) requires consumer reporting agencies to follow reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy of reported information.

- 15 U.S.C. 1681i requires credit reporting agencies to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation when a consumer disputes the accuracy or completeness of information.

The continued reporting of this foreclosure account without proper verification or documentation may constitute inaccurate and misleading reporting. I have not received sufficient evidence verifying the account, including foreclosure completion records, account history, and evidence that the reporting is accurate.

Therefore, I am requesting the following resolution : 1. A full reinvestigation of this mortgage foreclosure account.

2. Documentation verifying the foreclosure, including completion records, account history, and balance verification.

3. Documentation proving compliance with 15 U.S.C. 6802 ( b ) regarding disclosure of my financial information.

4. Immediate correction or deletion of this account from my credit report if the reporting can not be fully verified, documented, and legally justified.

If the furnisher can not provide sufficient verification and evidence supporting the continued reporting of this account, I request that it be removed from my credit report immediately and that all consumer reporting agencies be notified of the correction.

Once the property was sold, I intended to bring the other loan current and resume normal payments. 

At the time, I was not aware that Selene XXXX had a clause in the promissory note stating that if a payment becomes 31 days or more past due, the interest rate increases from 4 % to 22 %, and they will not accept partial payments. 

My last mortgage payment was made in XX/XX/XXXX. I repeatedly attempted to have Selene accept a partial payment but was unsuccessful. 

Because the property was already on the market, I decided to focus on completing the sale, accepting that I might incur the higher interest rate and late fees for a short period. 

I eventually secured a buyer, and the closing was originally scheduled for XX/XX/XXXX. However, due to delays caused by Selene XXXX, the closing did not occur until XX/XX/XXXX. 

Prior to closing, I requested a payoff statement from Selene XXXX. The payoff they provided incorrectly calculated interest from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, totaling 173 days of interest.

The correct interest period should have been XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, which equals 115 days. 

I made numerous phone calls to Selene XXXX attempting to have this error corrected. It was extremely difficult to get past the initial call representatives, who repeatedly stated that their system generated the payoff amount and they were unable to modify it. 

Eventually, I reached someone in Selenes Commercial Lending Department who acknowledged the issue, apologized, and provided an email address where I could submit documentation regarding the error. After reviewing my email, he responded with the timeline they used to calculate the interest. 

However, when Selene issued a corrected calculation, they changed the timeline to XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, which is still incorrect.

I also sent Selene XXXX a formal written complaint, but the response I received simply stated how much I received at closing and made no attempt to address or correct the interest calculation error. 

I am requesting that Selene XXXX : 1. Correct the payoff calculation to reflect the proper interest period. 
2. Refund the {$3600.00} in improperly charged interest. 
3. Refund the {$360.00} in additional interest caused by their delays. 
4. Provide a written explanation of how this error occurred. 

Despite numerous attempts to resolve this matter directly with Selene XXXX, they have failed to correct the error or return the funds they improperly collected.

I applied for a Guitar Center credit card issued by Synchrony Bank after being encouraged to do so by a cashier at a Guitar Center store. At the time of the purchase, the cashier told me that by opening the credit card I would receive rewards points worth approximately {$100.00}. I was specifically instructed to wait a couple of months and watch for an email containing the reward. 

Over the following months, I regularly checked my email, including my spam folder, but I never received any email or notification about a rewards certificate. I also searched online for information and asked another Guitar Center employee about it a few weeks later. I was again told to be patient and that the rewards email would eventually arrive. 

When no email ever appeared, I contacted Synchrony Bank through their online chat support. At that time, I was told that I had no rewards points on my account. The representative later explained that the {$100.00} reward had actually been issued as a certificate included in my XXXX credit card statement. By the time I learned this information, it was XX/XX/year>, and the reward certificate had already expired on XX/XX/year>. When I called Synchrony Bank to request that they honor or reissue the reward certificate, they refused. 

I believe I was misled by the Guitar Center cashier and by the way the rewards program information is presented. I was told to expect an email notification, but instead the certificate was placed only within a credit card statement without any clear or prominent notification. This made the reward very easy to miss. The reward also did not appear anywhere obvious in the Synchrony account interface when I logged in ; it was only accessible within the downloadable statement documents. 

This lack of clear disclosure and notification effectively hid the reward certificate and prevented me from using it before it expired. The {$100.00} reward was a primary reason I agreed to open the credit card at the time of purchase. Had I known that the reward would only appear buried within a statement without any notification, I would not have opened the account. 

I believe this practice is misleading to consumers and does not make the reward information reasonably accessible. I am requesting that Synchrony Bank reissue or honor the {$100.00} reward certificate that expired on XX/XX/year>. 

Why was my reward certificate not sent to me in an email as I was told? 
Why is the reward certificate and points not clearly indicated when I log into my account?

It is now several weeks later and this persons account is still active for pay anyone money transfers.
