I am filing a complaint against Innovate Loan Servicing / Innovate Auto Loan Servicing regarding failure to provide necessary title documentation for registration of my financed vehicle after moving to Florida.

I am still making payments on the vehicle, so Innovate is the lienholder and I do not hold the paper title. To register the vehicle in Florida, I requested the documentation required for an out-of-state title and lien situation. Florida advised that this can be satisfied by the lienholder providing either a copy of the out-of-state title or a lienholder letter on company letterhead identifying the vehicle and lien information. 

On XX/XX/year>, I emailed the Florida XXXX form to XXXX. I received no response. I then called the same day and was told to send the request to the titles department, which I did. 

On XX/XX/year>, Innovate responded with an attachment titled Paper Title Request Acknowledgement Document. That document states that a paper title was being requested from Texas. This was not the relief I requested, and it did not resolve my Florida registration issue. I later contacted Texas XXXX and was informed that because Innovate is the lienholder, Innovate is the party that needs to handle the title process and provide the necessary documentation. Texas XXXX indicated that this was not something I needed to do myself. 

After hearing nothing further, I followed up by email on XX/XX/year>, asking whether anything else was needed from me. I received no response. 

On XX/XX/year>, I emailed again and specifically asked for a lienholder letter stating that the Texas title had been requested and was pending transfer to Florida for registration purposes. I explained that I had a court date on XX/XX/year>, and asked that they at least provide a letter because the title process did not appear close to completion. The only prior response I had received from Innovate was an email from XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX stating : Attached is the title request receipt. We will send the title to the Florida Tax Collector at the address provided once it has been received. This still did not provide the actual documentation I needed. 

I then continued calling Innovate. At one point, I was placed on hold for a long time and told that something had been sent that day, around XX/XX/year>, but I received no confirming email, no tracking information, and no proof that the correct documentation had actually been sent. 

Most recently, on or about XX/XX/year>, I contacted Innovate again and spoke with the title department. I was told they might get to it that day or the next day. I also spoke with a customer service representative who checked outgoing mail activity and told me the last shipment reflected in their system was the earlier, incorrect item sent in connection with Texas. In other words, the correct Florida registration documentation still had not been sent. 

I have now been dealing with this issue for months. Because Innovate has failed to provide the correct documentation, I was pulled over and have had court appearances and continued legal problems related to my inability to complete Florida registration. This is especially frustrating because I have repeatedly tried to resolve the issue, I am still making payments, and the lender appears to be the only party with the ability to complete this process correctly. 

I am asking for immediate intervention. I want Innovate Loan Servicing to provide the correct title documentation required for Florida registration without further delay, and to confirm in writing exactly what was sent, when it was sent, and where it was sent.

4. Proof your company is authorized and licensed to collect in my state, including registration details.

5. Any notices or communications you claim you sent before reporting the account to the credit bureaus.

6. The identity and address of the original creditor, along with the original account details. 

XXXX. Evidence that the information you are furnishing follows accurate reporting standards and matches the data required by the FCRA and XXXX XXXX. 

I am asking for these items because I want to review real documentation, not summaries, screenshots, or general statements. If this account is legitimate, you should have no issue providing the paperwork needed to validate it. 
Until this information is provided, I am requesting that all collection activity pause as allowed under federal law. 
If you can not validate the account with proper documentation, I expect the tradeline to be removed from all credit reporting agencies. 
Lastly, I prefer that all communication from your office be in writing. Please do not call my phone or contact my job. Written correspondence only. 
Once I receive the requested documentation, I will review it within a reasonable timeframe and respond accordingly.

Subject : Formal Complaint Systemic Inaccurate Reporting and Failure of Credit Bureaus to Ensure Compliance To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint regarding a pattern of inaccurate and misleading credit reporting across multiple accounts furnished by various creditors and debt collectors, and the failure of the nationwide consumer reporting agencies to ensure compliance with federal law. 

The following furnishers are involved : XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 

Despite multiple disputes, these accounts continue to be reported inaccurately, including : Charged-off accounts reported as past due, creating a false impression of active delinquency Continuous monthly charge-off reporting for years, implying ongoing activity Balance updates without any payment activity Missing or inconsistent Date of First Delinquency ( DOFD ) Reporting that suggests extended or ongoing delinquency beyond actual charge-off dates Additionally, the nationwide consumer reporting agencies XXXX XXXX, and TransUnion have failed to conduct reasonable reinvestigations and have continued to report this information after disputes were submitted.

This conduct constitutes violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including : - 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) : Failure to ensure maximum possible accuracy - 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( FCRA 611 ) : Failure to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation - 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) : Failure of furnishers to properly investigate and correct disputed information For collection activity : - 15 U.S.C. 1692e : False, deceptive, or misleading representations The continued reporting of this information by both furnishers and credit reporting agencies creates a false and misleading impression of ongoing delinquency and has caused measurable harm to my credit profile.

This letter serves as a request for full debt validation pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) 15 U.S.C. 1681i.

I do not acknowledge this debt as valid. Before any further reporting, collection activity, or communication regarding this account continues, I am requesting that you provide the following : Verification of the debt, including the original signed contract or agreement bearing my signature. 

The complete payment history and itemized breakdown showing how the alleged balance was calculated. 

Proof of your legal authority to collect or report this debt, including a copy of any assignment or purchase agreement from the original creditor. 

The name, address, and contact information of the original creditor for proper verification.

Consumer complaint narrative:
My mortgage began to fall behind in XXXX XXXX XXXX I had to assist my mother in getting medication for a medical emergency that wasnt covered by her insurance. In XXXX, I attempt to start making payments and again but PPH Mortgage refused my payment stating that I had to make at least XXXX payments or their system would not allow for payment to be made. 
I told the associate I could not afford to make XXXX payments at that time. I was encouraged to apply for assistance. I started the process for assistance. I was then told it could take up to 30 days of review and if additional information was needed they would let me know. 
I found myself applying over and over again trying to get assistance. 
In late XXXX, I received a letter denying my request for a repayment plan. 
The reason for the denial was a modification had been provided less than XXXX months prior. 

I feel that it is unlawful for a mortgage company to stop accepting payments and present false hope regarding available assistance. I should have been told in XXXX, because you received assistance less than XXXX months ago, you are not eligible for a repayment plan or a modification. Instead I was lead to believe that assistance was available when it actually was not. 

For 6 months, I was led to believe that assistance was available when in actuality it was not. In XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX payments was approximately {$2800.00}. On the date that I was told Im ineligible for assistance, the balance is now owe over {$15000.00} including attorneys fees. 

I should have never been presented with an option for a repayment plan if I was not eligible. Im on the brink of being another homeless veteran and the representatives on the line are just reading their scripts. And they apologize for the misinformation. At some point when most of the associates are misinforming you its intentional and should be deemed mortgage malpractice. 

This is just XXXX area in which I was grossly misinformed. Ive been calling multiple times a week for several months. Each representative has a script that they read telling me as long as you are in active review for assistance, the foreclosure proceedings will be stalled. When I called today, the associate said you are in active foreclosure and your account is in final review for assistance. I confirmed that it was that I was still in review. Reiterated that at least XXXX people have said to me that as long as it is in a review status, the foreclosure is stalled. 

I have not been given the opportunity to make an informed decision or plan properly to save my home. They stopped taking my payment and then offered assistance that they never planned to give me. Yet they waited to tell me. They waited until the cost to reinstate the mortgage was so far out of reach that I may be forced out of my home. 

No one has answers everyone sticks to script they pretend to not have access to certain information but they clearly do. 

I am appalled that this is happening to me. PPH Mortgage / Onity Mortgage I guess is the new name. They should not be permitted to treat veterans or any citizen this way.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint regarding an ongoing XXXX insurance claim that has been unreasonably delayed due to improper documentation demands. 

My vehicle was involved in an accident and declared a total loss in XX/XX/year>. Since that time, I have been working with the company to process my XXXX claim. My insurance company and I have fully cooperated and provided all requested documentation, including : Buyers Order ( proof of purchase price ) Payment history ( provided directly by the finance company XXXX XXXX and loss documentation Despite this, the company continues to delay my claim by requesting a window sticker or MSRP invoice and stating they did not receive the payoff history. 

I want to clearly state the following : * I have provided the payoff history that XXXX XXXX sent me, more than once. 
* I do not have, and never had, a window sticker. 
* I purchased the car brand new, and their website has it as a " Used car purchase '' to minimize the value of my warranties. 
* I have requested they cancel the XXXX XXXX XXXX - Used - ( WHICH SHOULD BE LABELED NEW ). They have been notified and received records that the vehicle was involved in an accident and totaled in XXXX 2026. The warranty was NEVER used. 
* It is standard practice for dealerships to remove and discard the window sticker at the time of sale or vehicle delivery. 
* The buyers order is the legally recognized document reflecting the purchase price of the vehicle. 
* The companys own internal notes acknowledge receipt of the buyers order. 

The continued demand for a document that does not exist is unreasonable and appears to be a delay tactic. 

This claim has been ongoing for several months, and the repeated requests for unavailable documentation have prevented timely resolution.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing a complaint regarding Embassy Loan and the repossession and sale of my vehicle, a XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX. 

I fully owned this vehicle, having paid approximately {$65000.00} before taking out a title loan with a remaining balance of about {$5000.00}. The vehicle had under XXXX miles and was in overall good condition. The only issue was a XXXX control module, which temporarily prevented the vehicle from starting. This was a minor, repairable issue that I was actively in the process of fixing, and once repaired the vehicle would have been fully operational. 

Embassy Loan repossessed my vehicle and sold it for under {$6000.00}. This is a grossly undervalued price. Even in poor condition, this type of vehicle has an estimated value of around {$30000.00} based on industry standards such as XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

I did not receive any notice of the sale. I did not receive any mail, email, or phone communication prior to the sale, which deprived me of the opportunity to redeem my vehicle or protect my interest. 

After the sale, Embassy Loan is now claiming that I owe a remaining balance ( deficiency ), which I dispute in full. The sale was conducted in a commercially unreasonable manner and at a significantly undervalued price. 

I sent a formal written dispute requesting documentation and resolution, and I also contacted the company directly. I was told I would receive a response by email, but I have not received anything. 

I am seeking removal of the alleged deficiency balance, full documentation of the repossession and sale, and compensation for the difference between the vehicles fair market value and the amount it was sold for.

Key Account Details : Account/Furnisher : XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) XXXX Account Number : XXXX Original Creditor : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX account XXXX XXXX XXXX  or similar private-label financing used at XXXX XXXX ) Reported as : Collection account, opened XX/XX/XXXX, as of XX/XX/XXXX Current Balance Shown : {$5100.00} ( both current and original balance ) Payment History : Multiple C ( collection ) marks in XXXX Facts of the Case : This debt originated from financing at XXXX XXXX through XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX under the XXXX XXXX  program. After payoff, a small residual interest notice of {$2.00} appeared, for which I have an email confirmation of payment directly to XXXX XXXX XXXX  ( XXXX ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. 
Despite the debt being fully satisfied with the original creditor in XXXX, XXXX placed it as a new collection in XX/XX/XXXX with the full {$5100.00} balance still showing. I filed multiple disputes with XXXX requesting debt validation ( proof of ownership, chain of title from XXXX XXXX XXXX, accurate balance after my XXXX payoff, etc. ). XXXX failed to provide adequate validation and continued reporting the account as open/unpaid. XXXX has a documented pattern of consumer complaints for failing to properly validate debts under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) 1692g ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ) and for inaccurate reporting practices. 
I then filed multiple disputes directly with XXXX ( via the app/site ), providing details of the XXXX full payoff via the six money orders payable to the order of First Electronic Bank XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX the {$2.00} payment email confirmation to First Electronic Bank XXXX and information about XXXX  failure to validate the debt.

I am submitting this complaint regarding the reporting practices of Affirm, which I believe are unfair and do not reasonably reflect my current financial standing or circumstances. 

I previously contacted Affirm directly to request a goodwill adjustment for negative reporting associated with my account. This request was made in good faith due to financial hardship I experienced during a period of medical leave, which temporarily affected my ability to maintain timely payments. Despite this, I have since taken full responsibility for the account and have made consistent efforts to maintain good standing. 

Affirm denied my request without demonstrating that my individual situation was meaningfully reviewed. Their response appeared to be automated and did not address the hardship I explained. This raises concerns about whether consumers are being given fair consideration when requesting reasonable adjustments. 

The continued reporting of these negative marks is significantly impacting my credit profile and my ability to access fair credit and housing opportunities, even though my financial situation has improved and I am currently meeting my obligations. 

I am requesting that Affirm conduct a proper review of my account and remove or adjust the negative reporting in light of my demonstrated hardship and subsequent positive payment behavior. At a minimum, I am requesting a detailed explanation of how my request was evaluated and why it was denied. 

I believe consumers deserve fair and individualized consideration, especially when they have made good-faith efforts to resolve their accounts.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Subject/Issue Type : Inaccurate information on my consumer report Late payments and repossession-related entries reported incorrectly on a paid-in-full and closed auto loan ; Equifax failed to conduct a reasonable investigation of my disputes ( FCRA violation ). 

I am filing this complaint against Equifax Information Services LLC regarding an inaccurate collection tradeline and negative payment history furnished by XXXX XXXX XXXX that continues to appear on my Equifax credit report for my closed auto loan ( account XXXX ). 

Key Account Details : Account/Furnisher : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Account Number : XXXX Original Creditor/Lender : XXXX XXXX XXXX Auto Loan Reported as : Auto loan with multiple inaccurate late payments ( XXXX and XXXX delinquencies ), even though payments were made on time ; repossession-related entries stemming from XXXX incident. 
Status : Paid in full and closed as of XX/XX/XXXX ( original balance {$36000.00}, opened XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX term ). 
Facts of the Case : My auto loan with XXXX XXXX XXXX is paid in full and closed as of XX/XX/XXXX. Despite this, my Equifax report shows inaccurate negative information, including multiple red XXXX and XXXX late-payment entries ( e.g., XXXX XXXX, several in XXXX, and XXXX XXXX ). 
In XXXX, XXXX repossessed my vehicle due to a reported lapse of insurance. However, the insurance was paid on Friday, and the repossession occurred Friday night or early Saturday morning because XXXX  internal system failed to update appropriately to reflect the timely insurance payment. As a result of this wrongful repossession, I was forced to pay the repossession fee plus over {$5000.00} for recovery of the vehicle. 
DATCUs core systems, database, and system timing records failed to properly update the insurance payment and payment status. This does not adhere to the following regulations : FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) & ( a ) ( 2 ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ) Failure to maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy and furnishing of inaccurate information.

FCRA 623 ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) ) Failure to properly investigate and correct after disputes. 
XXXX Records Preservation Program ( 12 CFR Part 749 ) Records must accurately reflect information and be reconstructible ; system failures preventing timely updates violate this. 
XXXX Credit Union Record Retention and Preservation ( 7 Tex. Admin. Code 91.405 ) Records must be kept in sufficient detail for examination, audit, and verification ; significant loan/collateral records must be retained XXXX years with accuracy. 
CFPB UDAAP Authority ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 ) Unfair acts or practices in auto servicing, including wrongful repossessions and inaccurate reporting caused by system breakdowns ( as detailed in CFPB Supervisory Highlights, Fall XXXX and XXXX ). 
I filed multiple disputes with the bureaus, providing details of the full payoff, the XXXX insurance payment timing, the wrongful repossession and recovery costs, and information about DATCUs system failures. Equifax must properly investigate this dispute as required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) 1681i ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ), which mandates a reasonable reinvestigation, forwarding of all relevant consumer information to the furnisher, and deletion or correction of inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable information ( usually within XXXX  days ). Equifax must also follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy of information as required by FCRA 1681e ( b ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ).

This failure mirrors the CFPBs XX/XX/XXXX consent order against Equifax for improper investigations of consumer disputes, in which Equifax was ordered to pay a {$15.00} XXXX penalty for ignoring consumer-submitted evidence, allowing improper reinsertion of deleted inaccuracies, providing confusing investigation results, and using flawed processes that affected millions of consumers in violation of the FCRA. 

Harm Caused : These inaccuracies, combined with the wrongful repossession and associated costs ( repossession fee + over {$5000.00} recovery ), are damaging my credit score and limiting my ability to obtain new credit, loans, or favorable interest rates. The reported late payments and repossession-related entries continue to appear negatively even though the loan is paid in full and closed, and the issues stemmed from DATCUs own internal system failures. 

What I Want Resolved : Immediate deletion or full correction of the inaccurate late-payment entries and repossession-related information from my Equifax credit report. 
Confirmation in writing from Equifax that the items have been permanently removed or corrected and will not be reinserted. 
Any other corrective action required under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and related regulations. 
I have attached the screenshots from my XXXX  report showing the Paid, Closed status alongside the red late-payment entries and pink warning banner ( the same inaccurate information appears or should be checked on Equifax ) . I am in the process of locating additional XXXX repo and insurance records and will provide them upon request. 

I request that the CFPB investigate this matter and require Equifax to correct my report. I am available for any additional information needed. 

Thank you. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XX/XX/XXXX 2026

The Issue : Improper debt collection and failure to process a contractually mandated insurance claim ( XXXX XXXX XXXX  ). 
Description : I am a former account holder of a credit union ( Original Creditor ) where I was enrolled in a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX '' ( Plan # XXXX ) covering life, disability, and involuntary unemployment, effective XX/XX/XXXX. In XXXX, I experienced a qualifying hardship ( involuntary unemployment/disability ) while this coverage was active. 
The Original Creditor has admitted in writing ( Ref :! XXXX ) that my coverage was active until XX/XX/XXXX, which encompasses the date of my hardship. Despite this, the Original Creditor failed to initiate the claim process and instead charged off and sold the debt to a third-party debt buyer. 
I am now being sued by a law firm representing the debt buyer in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. I have attempted to resolve this through the Original Creditors Executive Correspondence office, but they have placed me in a " circular loop '' : they direct me to the insurer, while the insurer states the Original Creditor must verify the eligibility period and initiate the claim as the policyholder. 
On XX/XX/XXXX, I served a formal Demand and Cease & Desist via certified mail ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) to the legal firm representing the debt buyer, notifying them of the insurance dispute. They have failed to respond and continue to pursue legal action for a debt that should have been satisfied by the insurance policy I paid for. 
Requested Resolution : Immediate stay of all legal proceedings by the debt buyer and their legal counsel.

The Original Creditor must fulfill its obligation to initiate and process the claim with the plan administrator for the XXXX coverage period.

In approximately XXXX, XXXX, I contacted XXXX XXXX customer service regarding my credit card account. I was experiencing financial difficulty and inquired about payment options.

Consumer complaint narrative:
b'Portfolio Recovery Associates, LLC ("PRA"), through its collection counsel XXXX XXXX XXXX, is attempting to collect an alleged debt of $XXXX. PRA claims this alleged debt originated with XXXX XXXX XXXX. as an account ending XXXX. The PRA reference number is XXXX.

On XX/XX/XXXX, I mailed PRA a written dispute letter by USPS certified mail. The letter set forth twelve specific validation demands under 15 U.S.C.  1692g and 12 C.F.R.  1006.34 (Regulation F), including: (1) verification the alleged debt is valid; (2) original creditor name and address; (3) a signed cardholder agreement; (4) complete account statements from origination; (5) itemization of the alleged $XXXX balance; (6) the date of first delinquency; (7) chain of title and bill of sale from XXXX XXXX XXXX. to PRA; (8) proof of assignment of the specific alleged account; (9) legal authority for interest and fee accrual on an alleged charged-off account; (10) Utah licensing or registration proof; (11) attorney-review verification under 15 U.S.C.  1692e(3); and (12) the consumer rights notice.

PRA responded on XX/XX/XXXX with a form letter and a single month's account statement. That response left ten of the twelve specific validation demands entirely unaddressed. It did not include the cardholder agreement, chain of title, bill of sale, itemization, licensing proof, or attorney-review verification.

On XX/XX/XXXX, I mailed a follow-up insufficiency letter by USPS certified mail to XXXX XXXX XXXX  (tracking XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX) and to PRA at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX CA XXXX (tracking XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX). Both letters were delivered.

As of today, XX/XX/XXXX, thirty-six days have passed since the XX/XX/XXXX insufficiency letter. Neither PRA nor XXXX XXXX has provided the validation information specifically demanded. Under 15 U.S.C.  1692g(b), a debt collector "shall cease collection of the debt, or any disputed portion thereof, until the debt collector obtains verification of the debt . . . and a copy of such verification . . . is mailed to the consumer." Silence is not verification.

During that same period, interest of $XXXX has continued to accrue on the alleged charged-off balance (from $XXXX to $XXXX), which raises a potential 15 U.S.C.  1692f(1) violation  collection of an amount not authorized by the agreement creating the alleged debt or permitted by law.

Separately, XXXX XXXX XXXX.  the original alleged creditor  sent me electronic notifications titled "you're current on an account" on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX, three consecutive days. XXXX XXXX also sent a letter dated XX/XX/XXXX referencing an account ending XXXX (not the alleged PRA account ending XXXX). XXXX XXXX own records appear inconsistent with PRA's representation that the alleged account ending XXXX was charged off and sold to PRA.

PRA has been the subject of two prior CFPB consent orders  a $XXXX XXXX  order in XXXX and a $XXXX XXXX order in XXXX  both addressing inadequate validation and false representations regarding consumer debts. The conduct described in this complaint follows the same pattern.

I am concurrently filing formal FCRA  1681i disputes with XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX, and I have sent litigation-hold preservation letters to PRA, JXXXX XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX XXXX.

The alleged debt remains formally disputed. It has been disputed continuously since XX/XX/XXXX. PRA has not provided adequate validation. Despite that, PRA and XX/XX/XXXX have continued collection activity.'
